name: swift-ios-feature-commit-workflow
description: End-to-end workflow for implementing a Swift/SwiftUI iOS feature using the cortex plan→implement→review→commit pipeline, including GRDB persistence, URLSession actor networking, and Swift 6.2 strict concurrency compliance.
when_to_use: When implementing a new feature for the EPD-iOS app following the cortex workflow: route addition, DTO/domain model, use case, repository, view model, SwiftUI view, unit tests, commit.
workflow_sequences: implement: Route case → DTO → domain model → Endpoint → UseCase → Repository → ViewModel(@Observable @MainActor) → SwiftUI View(.task) → unit tests → xcodebuild test
commit: pipeline_handoff(init) → run_quality_gate() → git add <files> → git commit
example_invocations: Implement CounterpartyDetails remote layer: DTO, endpoint, use case, profile screen, 18 files, BUILD SUCCEEDED Swift 6.2.
Implement Documents feature: DocumentFilter, DocumentDetails, DocumentScanner stub, 11 Swift files, 12 unit tests.
troubleshooting_tips: Swift 6.2 strict concurrency: mark all ViewModels @MainActor, use async/await, avoid Sendable violations.
GRDB: run migrations in AppDatabase.migrator, use DatabaseQueue actor for isolation.
URLSession actor: all network calls go through NetworkService actor, never directly in ViewModels.
Route additions require both an enum case in Route.swift and a switch arm in RouteDestinationView.
Always run xcodebuild tests before committing: xcodebuild test -scheme EPD-Dev -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16'.
